title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Doctor's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Body and Symptoms, Measurements and Clues, Cells and Systems, Safety and Evidence, Clinical Reasoning across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues carefully.
Test your medical knowledge.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Body and Symptoms, Measurements and Clues, Cells and Systems, Safety and Evidence, Clinical Reasoning. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a medical-school admission exam, professional qualification, diagnosis or medical advice. Seek qualified medical care for personal symptoms or emergencies.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

answers.a1: Relevant past and present health information

doctor-round1-new2.question: Which structure carries urine from a kidney toward the bladder?

answers.a1: An experience reported by the patient

doctor-q4.question: In a classic presentation of appendicitis, abdominal pain may move toward which area?

answers.a1: Considering possible explanations for the findings

doctor-round2-new4.question: Why does the timing of symptoms matter?

doctor-q8.question: What is the functional filtering unit of the kidney called?

doctor-round4-new1.question: Why should a patient's medication allergies be checked?

answers.a4: To guarantee that no side effect can occur

answers.a1: A reason a treatment may be unsuitable or unsafe

doctor-round4-new3.question: A patient suddenly deteriorates during assessment. What is the general priority?

answers.a1: Seek urgent help and assess immediate threats
answers.a3: Wait until the next planned appointment

doctor-round4-new4.question: What is the purpose of informed consent?

answers.a1: Supporting a voluntary decision based on relevant information

doctor-q9.question: A person is unresponsive and not breathing normally. What is the safest immediate general response?

answers.a1: Call emergency services and begin appropriate basic life support
answers.a2: Wait several minutes for spontaneous recovery
answers.a4: Ask the person to walk around

doctor-q10.question: Which statement about antibiotics is most accurate?

answers.a2: They do not treat viral infections such as the common cold
answers.a3: They should always be stopped as soon as symptoms improve
answers.a4: They work by lowering body temperature directly

doctor-round5-new2.question: Can one abnormal test result establish every possible diagnosis by itself?

answers.a1: No; it must be interpreted in clinical context
answers.a3: Yes; all abnormal values mean the same disease
answers.a4: No; abnormal results are never useful

doctor-round5-new3.question: What does a negative test result mean when a test is imperfect?

answers.a1: It may reduce suspicion without ruling out the condition completely
answers.a2: It guarantees the condition is impossible
answers.a4: It means the sample was always invalid

doctor-round5-new4.question: Why compare a patient's current findings with earlier measurements?

answers.a2: To avoid speaking to the patient
answers.a3: To guarantee the old diagnosis still applies
